cost_usd.note: the script's own live computation showed $0.0000 due to a cap_scope/run_id mismatch bug in THIS calibration script: run_id="calibration-refdate" does not start with cap_scope="calibration-refdate-" (trailing hyphen), so ledger.scoped_usd() found zero matching entries. The $0.02 cap was still actively enforced throughout by the provider proxy's own separate, in-process ProxyState.spent_usd/check() mechanism (scripts/arena/provider_proxy.py), which is independent of the ledger cap_scope string match -- confirmed no overspend risk existed, only a reporting bug. Real cost recomputed directly from the 4 ledger lines this run wrote.

unexpected_findings: The extracted fact text is byte-identical between BASE and TREATMENT: "Took a red-eye flight on JetBlue from San Francisco to Boston today" in both arms. The relative word "today" is preserved verbatim, NOT resolved to an absolute date, even though the TREATMENT system prompt correctly states "Today's date is 2022-11-17."

Re-reading the actual (correctly version-matched) 1.0.6 prompt text confirms why: USER_MEMORY_EXTRACTION_PROMPT states the current date as a bare contextual fact but contains NO instruction telling the model to use it to convert relative time expressions in extracted facts. Its few-shot examples actively demonstrate the opposite: "Yesterday, I had a meeting..." -> ["Had a meeting with John at 3pm..."] with "Yesterday" simply dropped, not converted. The patch supplies a correct anchor date; it does not supply an instruction to use it.
Calibration script itself had a cap_scope/run_id trailing-hyphen mismatch (see cost_usd.note); did not affect actual spend enforcement, did affect this script's own live cost reporting.
